thread:
Maya (SRE): Quick heads-up — we've detected correlated ECC/Xid errors and thermal warning events on 4 GPUs in the eu-west dedicated pool. Auto-drain triggered for 3 hosts. Need customer-facing language and confirmation of timing for outreach.

Alex (CS): Thanks Maya. Can you summarize impact (affected customers, capacity delta, ETA on replacement) so we can draft comms? Who will own the notifications?

Jin (Infra): Short version: probable failing fan controller + intermittent PCI/NVLink errors causing soft Xid 79 and occasional kernel rebinds. Diagnostics captured: hw logs + nvml dumps. Replacement path: swap cards and run soak tests. ETA for on-site swap (standard spare shipment) 24-48 hours; if expedited, ~12-24h but needs approval.

Jin (Infra): Capacity impact: the eu-west dedicated pool will temporarily lose ~6-9% peak throughput while drained hosts route workloads to reserve capacity. Autoscaling+burst handles most customer traffic; customers with pinned dedicated nodes may see degraded throughput for a window until replace. No evidence of data integrity issues; nothing surfaced in audit logs.

Sam (AM): Can we surface a short, non-alarming message to affected Dedicated/Private customers + an ops ticket with timeline and contact? I can own outreach for named accounts but need approved wording.

Priya (Legal): One note on wording: avoid definitive statements about "hardware failure caused data loss" unless we've confirmed. Recommend phrase: "we observed hardware errors affecting GPUs which triggered automatic failover. We are replacing hardware and monitoring for any impact." Also include contact & support escalation path.

Alex (CS): Draft below (short):

"Proposed customer note (for Dedicated/Private customers in eu-west):
Hi — we want to let you know we observed GPU hardware errors affecting a small number of nodes in the eu-west dedicated pool that triggered automatic failover. Impact: you may notice reduced throughput or longer queue times for requests pinned to affected hosts. What we're doing: we've drained the affected hosts, routed workloads to healthy capacity, and dispatched hardware replacement. ETA for full restoration is 24–48 hours (we'll update sooner if expedited). What you need to do: no action required on your side; if you have pinned hardware or specific SLA requirements, contact your account manager and we'll prioritize. Contact: support@redwood.ai / your AM.

Proposed footer: "We take hardware reliability seriously; we will follow up with a post-incident summary including cause and mitigation steps."

Alex (CS): Thoughts? Priya ok with that language?

Priya (Legal): That reads fine; just change "we'll update sooner if expedited" -> "we will provide updates as we have them" (avoids promising faster). Also add: "no evidence of data exposure has been found" — only if Jin confirms.

Jin (Infra): Confirming: no evidence of data exposure in audit or kernel logs. I can add a small log excerpt for internal post-incident but not in the customer note.

Maya (SRE): Operational note: our monitoring will push alerts if drain completes or if additional hosts show the pattern. Suggested send window: within 2 hours so customers know we've acknowledged and are working it. Also propose adding a short FAQ line for pinned reservations and Dedicated SLAs.

infra-monitor (bot): infra-monitor: drained host gpu-09-eu1 at 2026-03-05T10:12:34Z (reason: ECC/Xid errors)

Sam (AM): I'll prep the account list and queue emails once wording is final. Suggest parallel path: broad notification to all eu-west dedicated customers + targeted follow-ups to pinned accounts.

Alex (CS): Final draft with legal tweak:

"Customer notice (send to affected Dedicated/Private customers):
Hello — we want to make you aware that we observed hardware-level GPU errors on a small number of nodes in the eu-west dedicated pool which triggered automatic failover. Impact: you may experience reduced throughput for workloads running on pinned hosts or slightly increased queueing while we route traffic.
What we're doing: affected hosts have been drained and workloads routed to healthy capacity. Hardware replacement is scheduled; we expect full restoration within 24–48 hours. We will provide updates as we have them.
What you can do: no action required. If your workloads require guaranteed capacity during the window, contact your account manager and we will coordinate options.
Contact: support@redwood.ai or your account manager.

Note: we have not found any evidence of data exposure. A post-incident summary will follow with cause and mitigation.

Alex (CS): @Sam can you confirm the list of impacted accounts and we'll schedule the send at 14:00 UTC? Also need sign-off from @Maya and @Priya.

Maya (SRE): sign-off for technical content. 14:00 UTC send window works for ops to have initial logs attached.

Priya (Legal): sign-off for legal phrasing.

Sam (AM): Working list ready, will queue drafts. I'll add a short customer-specific note for big accounts offering temporary capacity credits if they request. :thumbsup:

Jin (Infra): Ops plan: after card swap we run 6h soak + perf test, then mark host ready. If we see repeated errors on a replacement card, escalate to vendor for whole-board replacement.

Alex (CS): Great — proceeding with send at 14:00 UTC. Sam will own sends and follow-ups. I'll post the final copy to the support ticket template and the incident channel. Thanks everyone.

Maya (SRE): I'll keep monitoring and post updates here as drains/repairs progress.

infra-monitor (bot): infra-monitor: replacement task created for gpu-09-eu1 (ticket #INC-5482)

Alex (CS): Closing note: keep the customer updates concise, emphasize automatic failover and no evidence of data exposure, and offer AM contact for capacity needs.

Sam (AM): On it — will ping once sends are out."
